slides.title: Two Pointers
slides.main: A quadratic pair search becomes one pass when each pointer move guarantees something.

captions: Pointers from both ends close in: pair sum, container, palindrome
One reads, the other writes: compress the array in place
One pointer per sequence: merge, intersection, subsequence
Three forms, one principle: a pointer move guarantees something

body.text: Twenty exercises: half are interview classics.

slides.title: Inward: pair with a sum
slides.main: Too small: left right. Too big: right left. At most n steps.

captions: Target sum 10: left on the minimum, right on the maximum
Sum below target: the only way to raise it is to move left right
Above target: move right to the left
Too small again: left to the right
Met: 4 + 6 = 10. At most n steps: linear time

slides.title: Why the move is correct
slides.sub: Discard a candidate that is surely not needed
slides.main: Each step discards a candidate without losing the answer: explain it and the pointers are right.

captions: 1 + 11 = 12 exceeds target 10
Right element 11 with anyone to its left gives even more: no pair fits
11 can be discarded forever: the pointer moves with no loss
One candidate discarded per step: no need to check pairs

frames.text: n steps instead of n² pairs

slides.title: Container with water
slides.main: Move the shorter wall: moving the taller one is never better.

captions: Outer walls: max width, area by the smaller height: 8
Move the shorter (1): 8 and 7 give area 49, remember it
Now the shorter is the right one (7→3): area fell to 18
Move the shorter again: 40. Best stays 49. One pass

slides.title: Reader and writer
slides.sub: Compress an array on top of itself
slides.main: The writer never overtakes the reader: O(n) time, O(1) memory.

captions: Reader r visits all, writer w marks the spot for the next new value
Met a value different from the last written: write it, advance w
Equal values are simply skipped by the reader
The writer never overtakes the reader: compressed in one pass

frames.text: k = 3: the first k elements are the answer

slides.title: Array as a graph
slides.main: The cycle entry is the repeated number, with no array changes.

captions: From position i an arrow leads to a[i]. Two indices point to 2, so there is a cycle, and its entry is the duplicate
Tortoise and hare met inside the cycle (at position 4)
One pointer back to the start, both move one step
Met at the cycle entry: the repeated number is 2. O(1) memory, array untouched

frames.text: p1 from start, p2 from the meeting point

slides.title: Over two sequences
slides.main: Move the smaller pointer: O(n + m) steps.

captions: Two sorted arrays, one pointer on each
Equal: add to answer, move both
Equal again
Move the smaller pointer: it cannot find a pair further right in the other array
At most the sum of lengths: O(n + m)

slides.title: Triples
slides.main: Sort plus pointers: square instead of cube; skip duplicates.

captions: Sort and fix the first element; for the rest find a pair with sum “minus first”
For −1 the pair −1 and 2 fits
Pointers moved: the second triple is found
The next first element equals the previous one: skip it, or triples repeat

frames.text: −4 + (−1) + 2 = −3 < 0: no fitting third, no pairs for −4

slides.title: Dutch national flag
slides.main: Zeros left, twos right, ones between: the basis of quicksort partitioning.

captions: Three pointers: zeros before lo, twos after hi, mid sorts the unknown
Swap the two with hi and move only hi: the arrival is not yet examined
Swap the zero with lo: move both lo and mid
A one: just move on
One pass, O(n) time and O(1) memory. Quicksort partitioning is built on this

frames.text: start: 2 under mid, swap with the right boundary
swapped, hi − 1; mid stays: an unexamined element arrived

slides.title: Subsequence
slides.sub: One pointer on the short string, one on the long
slides.main: The pointer on s moves only when the next character is found.

captions: Pointer i walks the short string s, j walks the long one t
j runs past mismatches, i moves only when a character is found
Each character of t is visited once: O(|t|)
i reached the end: all characters of s found in order

frames.text: i at end of s: subsequence

slides.title: Counting pairs
slides.main: One comparison counts a whole range of pairs.

captions: Sorted array, count pairs with sum at most 7
One comparison counts all pairs of the left element with the range up to hi
Right is too big: move it; count the rest the same way
Nine pairs in one pass instead of a square; the price is the sort

frames.text: 1 + 6 = 7 ≤ 7: left fits with all to its right
+5 pairs. Now 2 + 6 = 8 > 7: right is too big

slides.title: Where it fails
slides.main: On unsorted data a move guarantees nothing: sort or use a hash.

captions: “Too big, move the right” holds only if larger values are on the right
Unsorted: 8 + 9 = 17 > 10, right dropped, and the answer 1 + 9 is lost
Sort first and the same reasoning works: 1 + 9 = 10
Need original indices? Sort (value, index) pairs or use a hash table

frames.text: order needed: else a move guarantees nothing

slides.title: Invariants and mistakes
slides.main: Keep an invariant: the answer lies between the pointers; every step moves at least one.

captions: Invariant: all left of lo and right of hi is discarded, answer in between
Loop condition: lo < hi. If lo == hi, a pair of an element with itself is invalid
If no branch moves a pointer, the loop is endless
Skip duplicates right after processing, with a bounds check

frames.text: branch without lo += 1 and hi -= 1 → endless loop
while lo < hi and a[lo] == a[lo+1]: lo += 1

slides.title: Summary and practice
slides.main: Inward, read and write, two sequences, plus sorting or hashing.

captions: Pair sum, container, palindrome: pointers close in
Duplicates, removal, zeros: the array compresses itself
Merge, intersection, subsequence
Needs monotonicity: sort or hash; watch bounds and duplicates
